paper_title: Direct Free Carrier Photogeneration in Single Layer and Stacked Organic Photovoltaic Devices
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2017 - Chandran - Direct Free Carrier Photogeneration in Single Layer and Stacked Organic Photovoltaic/auto/Advanced Materials - 2017 - Chandran - Direct Free Carrier Photogeneration in Single Layer and Stacked Organic Photovoltaic.md

knowledge_points.content: Subnaphthalocyanine chloride (SubNc) and subphthalocyanine chloride (SubPc) are identified as special bipolar semiconductors capable of direct free carrier generation upon photoexcitation without assistance from a P/N junction.
knowledge_points.evidence: These results confirm that SubNc and SubPc can directly generate free carriers upon photoexcitation without assistance from a P/N junction. ... SubNc and SubPc are indeed special bipolar semiconductors which are capable of generating direct free carriers upon photoexcitation.

knowledge_points.content: Single-layer photovoltaic devices using SubNc or SubPc as the active layer achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCE) of approximately 0.3%, which is 30 times higher than the typical 0.01% PCE reported for most single-layer organic devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: while PCEs of most single-layer OPV devices are extremely low (≈0.01%) PCEs of single-layer SubNc and SubPc devices are as high as 0.3% ... PCE in SubNc and the SubPc only devices are up to 0.3% which is more than 30 times higher than those of previously reported single layer devices.

knowledge_points.content: A single-layer device with the structure ITO/SubNc (20 nm)/BPhen (8 nm)/Al exhibits a short-circuit current density (JSC) of 2.7 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.02 V, a fill factor (FF) of 0.28, and a PCE of 0.8%.
knowledge_points.evidence: The SubNc/BPhen device shows a short circuit current density (Jsc), open circuit voltage (Voc), and fill factor (FF) of 2.7 mA cm−2 1.02 V and 0.28, respectively which accounts for a PCE of 0.8%.

knowledge_points.content: Bathophenanthroline (BPhen) is used as a 8 nm protecting layer in single-layer SubNc and SubPc devices to prevent the penetration of hot Aluminum atoms during thermal evaporation and to reduce charge carrier quenching.
knowledge_points.evidence: BPhen is used as a protecting layer that prevents hot Al penetration during metal deposition. ... These observed EQE reductions upon BPhen removal can be understood as the charge carrier quenching caused by the direct deposition of Al onto the active layers.

knowledge_points.content: SubNc and SubPc exhibit high real dielectric constant (ε1) values of 5.8 and 4.3, respectively, which facilitate the dissociation of electron-hole pairs into free carriers through efficient screening of Coulombic attraction.
knowledge_points.evidence: SubNc and SubPc exhibit relatively higher ε1 values of 5.8 and 4.3, respectively ... A high ε1 in organic materials can show efficient screening effect and thus facilitate the generation of free carriers.

knowledge_points.content: Spectroscopic ellipsometry measurements show that SubNc and SubPc have high refractive indices (n > 3) and extinction coefficients (k > 1.6), which are significantly higher than those of common materials like CuPc and C60.
knowledge_points.evidence: SubNc and SubPc exhibit significantly high n (> 3) and k (> 1.6) values comparing to CuPc and C60. ... These higher values of SubNc and SubPc are attributed to their molecular orientation and nonplanar cone shaped structures.

knowledge_points.content: The internal quantum efficiency (IQE) of bilayer SubNc/SubPc devices (approximately 50%) is found to be the sum of the IQEs of the individual single-layer devices (22% for SubNc and 26% for SubPc), indicating that the SubNc/SubPc interface has minimal influence on carrier dissociation.
knowledge_points.evidence: average IQEs for SubNc only, SubPc only, SubNc/ SubPc and SubPc/SubNc devices are estimated as 22% 26% 50% and 49%, respectively. Interestingly, average IQEs of bilayer devices (≈50%) are almost the sum of average IQEs of single layer devices (≈48%).

knowledge_points.content: Bilayer devices with reversed stacking sequences (SubNc/SubPc vs. SubPc/SubNc) exhibit nearly identical open-circuit voltages (VOC ≈ 0.55 V) and photovoltaic performance, confirming that the junction does not function as a typical P/N interface.
knowledge_points.evidence: Performances of these two devices are largely similar with Jsc, V∞, and FF )f ≈ 3 mA cm−2 ≈ 0.55 V and ≈ 0.30 ... In our experiment, reversing the organic junction has negligible influence on the Voc (Figure 2a). This is consistent with the model that the organic junction of SubNc/SubPc or SubPc/SubNc does not work as a typical D/A junction.

knowledge_points.content: An optimized bilayer device with the structure ITO/SubNc (12 nm)/SubPc (15 nm)/BPhen (8 nm)/Al achieves a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 3.2%, with a JSC of 6.6 mA/cm², VOC of 1.04 V, and FF of 0.46.
knowledge_points.evidence: Bilayer device with structure ITO/SubNc (12 nm)/SubPc (15 nm)/BPhen (8 nm)/Al has shown the highest PCE of 3.2% with a Jsc, Voc, and FF of 6.6 mA cm−2 1.04 V and 0.46% respectively.

knowledge_points.content: Organic films for these devices were deposited via thermal evaporation at a rate of 1-2 Å/s under high vacuum conditions (< 3 x 10^-6 Torr) on patterned ITO-coated glass substrates.
knowledge_points.evidence: Organic films were deposited through thermal evaporation at a deposition rate and a pressure of 1–2 Å s−1 and < 3 × 10−6 Torr, respectively.
